transcript:
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
The Supreme Court has for now revived a federal data system the Trump administration revamped
into a tool to check the citizenship of millions of registered voters.
As NPR's Jude Joffe Block reports, the tool had been used by some states before it was
blocked by a federal judge for violating privacy protections.
The federal tool is called SAVE, and the Trump administration made major changes to it last
year, including linking it to Social Security data for the first time.
But the tool has mistakenly flagged some U.S. citizens as potential non-citizens, leading
them to be taken off state voter rolls as a result.
A federal judge in June said the modified version of SAVE trampled on the privacy rights
of Americans and threatened the right to vote.
But the Supreme Court lifted that block and opened the door for the new SAVE tool to be
used in the lead-up to the election for individualized determinations of citizenship.
The law bars systematic purges of voter rolls this close to an election.
Jude Joffe Block, NPR News.
Record high diesel prices are putting a squeeze on loggers in the Pacific Northwest.
NPR's Kirk Singler reports this comes as President Trump has been using executive orders to try
and cut regulations that revive the struggling industry.
Diesel here in the timberlands of western Oregon is approaching $7 a gallon.
And loggers might have to drive 100 miles every morning to the job, you know.
They're meeting the crummy at 3 a.m.
Sean Smith owns Starfire Lumber, where logging trucks pull up daily after cutting trees on
nearby private and federal lands.
The dozers and shovels and yarders and stuff they run consume ungodly amounts of fuel.
I mean, you'll see 12 or 1,500-gallon tanker trailers at the logging site.
Smith says the industry is grappling with record diesel prices due to the closure of
the Strait of Hormuz, which is making inflation even worse just as lumber prices were starting
to recover.
Kirk Singler, NPR News, Eugene, Oregon.
It's that time again for students and families hoping to get federal help paying for college.
It's time to fill out the form known as the FAFSA, NPR's Corey Turner reports.
It stands for the Free Application for Federal Student Aid, and it's the gateway not just
to federal loans and grants, but also to a lot of state and even school-based financial
aid.
It is supposed to open on October 1st, but for the second year in a row, the Trump administration
has posted the form ahead of schedule.
In 2020, Congress moved to simplify the FAFSA, and in 2023, the Biden administration failed
to release the new and approved form on time, falling months behind schedule and sending
families and schools into a panic.
The Trump administration has made a few changes to this year's form, including making it shareable
between family members by text and getting rid of confusing jargon.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
U.S. stocks rose today after a cool-down in oil prices.
This is NPR News.
A new report on Charlie Kirk's assassination last year says his Turning Point USA organization
insisted he speak outdoors despite security concerns, and the university where he was
killed didn't properly assess dangers like the possibility of a rooftop shooter.
Those were among the key findings in an after-action report released by Utah Valley University.
A slow-moving nor'easter is sent to hammer the mid-Atlantic and New England, with damaging
winds, coastal flooding and heavy rain through Monday.
NPR's John Stoleness reports the storm is also wreaking havoc on the final weekend of
Major League Baseball's schedule.
As the city of Boston prepares to weather the storm, the hometown Red Sox will try to
squeeze in an important series against the Chicago Cubs.
Sunday's game was moved to today, with the two teams playing a double-header.
The start time of the second game was also moved up a half-hour, and they hope to get
a game in on Saturday night as well.
The Cubs are in a tight playoff race, so should any games be rained out, they will have to
be made up, either on Monday or Tuesday.
In Baltimore, Saturday's game between the Orioles and Yankees has been rescheduled.
Those two teams are also playing a double-header today.
No changes are likely for series being played in Philadelphia or Washington, D.C.
John Stoleness, NPR News.
Pope Leo XIV has warned that a paradise of machines could undermine humanity.
He's been raising concerns about AI, nuclear arms and human rights during his visit to
France.
Speaking to President Emmanuel Macron and others, Leo affirmed the Vatican's opposition
to nuclear weapons and emphasized peace through dialogue.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Supreme Court revives Trump administration's SAVE voter citizenship check tool despite privacy concerns
Record high diesel prices squeeze logging industry in Pacific Northwest as Trump pushes deregulation
FAFSA form for federal college aid opens early again under Trump administration with simplifications
U.S. stocks rise following cooldown in oil prices
Report finds Turning Point USA insisted Charlie Kirk speak outdoors despite security concerns
Nor'easter threatens mid-Atlantic and New England with damaging winds, flooding and heavy rain
Major League Baseball playoff teams reschedule games ahead of nor'easter hitting eastern seaboard
Pope Leo XIV warns artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons threaten humanity during France visit
